subject: THZ3 boss/support audit and $1B/$28 closure

evidence_classes.DECODED DATA: ROM tables/records decoded by a parser
evidence_classes.BYTE-VERIFIED ASSEMBLY: routine bytes compared literally and disassembled
evidence_classes.SOURCE-TRACED BEHAVIOR: behavior read from the disassembly, not executed
evidence_classes.CONTROLLED ROUTINE RESULT: original routine executed on a Z80 core with explicit RAM (tools/oracle.py)
evidence_classes.EMULATED ORIGINAL FRAME: whole original game run in the approximate SMS harness, update-aligned (see harness_note)

harness_note: The legacy `Emu.restore()` of tools/platform_spike_collision.py snapshots the machine at an arbitrary CPU position and does not restore `int_disabled`, `frame_tick` and `index_rp_kind`, so the FIRST update after a teleport can run a partially executed update and depends on IRQ phase (observed: vx -1004 versus -1024 for the same teleport). Every EMULATED fixture in this study therefore applies its writes from a PC hook at $1336 (the instruction after `CALL $062D` in the main loop $1333, i.e. exactly the start of a game update), so each update runs complete and repeated runs are bit-identical.

a1_cooldown_side_wall.evidence: BYTE-VERIFIED ASSEMBLY (helper $32CFD, scheduler $5DD1, merge $64CB) + CONTROLLED ROUTINE RESULT (real $1B callbacks)

answer.damage_cooldown: object +$1F = 16 after a damaging top contact; decremented once per helper call (states 1 and 2 only, +$04 bit 6 clear); frozen in states 3/4 and while asleep; it is not cleared by the cycle, so a remainder carries into the next raised phase
answer.contact_detection: the whole contact helper $32CFD returns before `CALL $033B` while the cooldown is non-zero: $6328 is not run, +$20/+$21 and the player's $D521 are not written for the 16 cooldown updates
answer.side_wall_response: NOT active during the cooldown: the wall is only the merged copy of $D521 (scheduler $5DD1 zeroes $D521 at the start of every object phase, $6328 is the only writer, merge $64CB copies it into $D523 for the next player pass); no $6328 call means no wall bit. It also requires a non-attacking, non-invulnerable player (merge gate)
answer.grounded_attacker_push: NOT active during the cooldown for the same reason (push code sits after the $033B call); it is an alternative to the wall because attackers are not merged
answer.does_the_cooldown_disable_the_whole_obje: No for the object itself (state script, movement, rise/hold/retract, rendering and +$04 handling continue); yes for everything the helper does (top damage, side wall and push)

a2_grounded_push.evidence: BYTE-VERIFIED ASSEMBLY ($32D2B..$32D58) + CONTROLLED ROUTINE RESULT (real states 1 and 2 callbacks)
a2_grounded_push.map_legend: rows dy -30..+30, columns dx -30..+30; D damage (top cone), R pushed to objX+23, L pushed to objX-23, . nothing; grounded attacker, vy >= 0, Sonic extents 8x24 (key '8') and 9x24 (key '9')

independence.varied: player byte $D504 (all residues of 5), X speed (0, +3.0, -3.0), object +$04 (0, mirror $10, $02, $80); ten positions
independence.result: push position, requested state, X speed and damage request never change: facing, speed sign and object orientation are not read

rule.applies_when: cooldown 0, +$04 bit 6 clear, state 1 or 2, player Y speed >= 0, $6328 contact bit is not 'player above' (bit 0), $D522 bit 1 AND $D503 bit 1 (grounded attacker)
rule.result: requested state 1, X speed 0, X := objX + 23 when contact bit 2 (horizontal-dominated, dx >= 0) else objX - 23; Y untouched; no damage
rule.contact_from_below: a vertical-dominated 'player below' contact (dy 0..24, depth 24-dy <= horizontal depth 24-|dx|) clears the horizontal bits, so +$21 bit 2 is clear and the push is ALWAYS -23 (left), even for dx > 0
rule.horizontal_right: R iff contact bit 2: dx >= 0 and (24 - dx) < vertical depth (24 - |dy|, dy <= 24); ties go to the vertical axis (so dx == |dy| is vertical)
rule.horizontal_left: dx < 0 and (24 - |dx|) < vertical depth: -23; the dx = 0 column is on the right-hand branch (dx >= 0)
rule.extent_9_state_0F: extents 9 shift the horizontal depth by one (key '9' map); the rule is unchanged
rule.after_push: the player callback of the next update applies requested state 1 ($45B3 clears $D503 bit 1): the roll ends; no other speed is touched
rule.poc_assumption_check: POC '-23 from below' is correct for below-contact; the +23 case exists only for horizontal-dominated right-side contact

a3_lifecycle.evidence: EMULATED ORIGINAL FRAME (THZ1, update-aligned) + SOURCE-TRACED BEHAVIOR (scheduler $5DD1, $61E1, $5EF8, platform $8908, spike $32C8B)

lift_28.phase_reading: the lift's Y at a fixed absolute update differs with the arrival time and direction: the phase origin is the creation update, not the level clock (differences of tens of pixels in the table)

asleep_motion.reading: +$04 starts at $40 (asleep); state 0 -> 11 takes two updates; the lift moves 1 px/update from the third update while +$04 bit 6 is still set (callback $86DA and its keep-alive bit 1 do not depend on bit 6)

rule.creation: steady scrolling: map cell 2 only (anchor 32..96 px outside the visible band, scan every 4th update); level start/teleport: cells 0/1 as well (initial fill)
rule.state_11_phase: callback runs every update while the slot exists, asleep or awake: the Y path is a pure function of updates since creation (Y -1 px/update for 16 x aux1 updates, then reversing)
rule.keep_alive: state 11 sets +$04 bit 1: $61E1 does not delete it; $8908 deletes it (type $FE, token cleared, so it is recreated) when |playerX - x| >= 640 or |playerY - y| >= 672 (PLAYER_DIST, camera independent); the X limit was verified at 639/640 on both sides
rule.recreation: a deleted lift is recreated at the placement Y with a fresh counter (phase 0) when it re-enters cell 2 (or at the next level start)
rule.state_5_sag_platforms: stationary; no keep-alive bit, so deleted by $61E1 outside the lifetime window and recreated at rest; support needs +$04 bit 6 clear (awake), the sag counter lives only while awake
rule.different_phase_on_arrival: yes: phase depends on the update at which the placement was created (arrival time/direction) and is reset by deletion

spike_1b.reading_creation: created asleep in cell 2 (state 0, +$04 = $40) and parked in state 1 (callback returns while asleep): the rise does not start until $61E1 clears bit 6 (about 9..29 updates later depending on scroll speed); the 102-update cycle therefore starts at WAKE, not at creation
spike_1b.reading_sleep: while asleep (bit 6 set, awake margin left) the scripts' own timers keep running but the callbacks are skipped: a spike put to sleep in the raised phase finishes its 48-update hold asleep, parks in state 3 raised at Y 846 and retracts only after waking; a long enough sleep desynchronises it from any fixed clock

rule.creation: steady scrolling: cell 2 only (outer ring, asleep); initial fill/teleport: cells 0/1 as well
rule.initial_state: state 0 callback $32C7D: +$03 bit 7, requested state 1, cooldown 0; the first rise happens after the first awake update
rule.script_vs_callback: states 2 (raised hold) and 4 (hidden hold) are timed by the object script (48 updates, runs asleep); states 1 (rise, 3 x 6 px) and 3 (retract) are advanced by callbacks that return while +$04 bit 6 is set
rule.lifetime: no keep-alive bit: deleted by $61E1 beyond the generic lifetime window (LEFT-96/RIGHT+96, token cleared -> recreated) and restarted from state 0/1 at the placement Y
rule.different_phase_on_arrival: yes: phase origin is the wake update after (re)creation; sleep/wake episodes shift it; deletion restarts it
rule.widescreen: the POC's post-wake retention adapter (max(0, view-256)) keeps a spike alive where the SMS would delete and restart it, so backtracking in the wide view can show a different phase than the original; at 256 px it is identical

a3_lifecycle.relation_to_viewport_audit: uses the generic lifetime of docs/viewport-semantics-audit.md unchanged (create cell 2 / initial fill, awake band [-32, 288), delete outside the [-96, 352) ring window, +$04 bit 1 keep-alive); the only $28/$1B-specific facts are the keep-alive radius 640x672 (PLAYER_DIST) and the callback gating above

a4_static_spike_aligned.evidence: EMULATED ORIGINAL FRAME (THZ1, update-aligned replay of the diagnostic grid of docs/platform-spike-collision-audit.md section 2.3)
a4_static_spike_aligned.harness_note: The legacy `Emu.restore()` of tools/platform_spike_collision.py snapshots the machine at an arbitrary CPU position and does not restore `int_disabled`, `frame_tick` and `index_rp_kind`, so the FIRST update after a teleport can run a partially executed update and depends on IRQ phase (observed: vx -1004 versus -1024 for the same teleport). Every EMULATED fixture in this study therefore applies its writes from a PC hook at $1336 (the instruction after `CALL $062D` in the main loop $1333, i.e. exactly the start of a game update), so each update runs complete and repeated runs are bit-identical.

first_update_rule.teleport_semantics: Emu.place() writes the REQUESTED state ($D502) only; the current state $D501 stays 1 (stand) for the first update, the engine applies the request at the start of that update
first_update_rule.update_1: airborne X speed |vx| > $0400 is clamped to +-$0400 (no drag that update); |vx| <= $0400 gets -16/256 drag toward 0 per update (observed -1024 -> -1008, +512 -> +496); gravity adds +48/256 to Y speed per update
first_update_rule.evidence: rows in legacy_ten_cases_replayed (three case families: vx -6 and -4 px, +2 px) and the aligned class table

a4_static_spike_aligned.interpretation: The six unresolved cases are the six E1 rows (rising teleports with vx -6/-4). Their difference from the older runs was the unaligned first update (vx -1004 instead of -1024 for the first -4 case, and x advancing 2 px instead of 1 px for the +2 px E2 rows), not different ROM behaviour. With update-aligned replay the rows are reproducible; the E2 set moves to the x >= 1564, vx +4 starts (leaving the 64 px block in one step); every other class is unchanged within 2% of runs.
